bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第055卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 55.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 55.

sentences.zh: 【漢紀四十七】　起閼逢執徐，盡柔兆敦牂，凡三年。

translations.literal: 【Han Records 47】 Beginning from Yanyu Zhixu through Rouzhao Dunzhang—in all, three years.
translations.idiomatic: 【Han Records 47】 From the first year of the Yanyu cycle through the last year of the Rouzhao cycle—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 春，二月，丙戌，邟鄉忠侯黃瓊薨。

translations.literal: In spring, the second month, on the day bingxu, Loyal Marquis Huang Qiong of Hangxiang died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the second month, on bingxu day, Loyal Marquis Huang Qiong of Hangxiang died.

sentences.zh: 將葬，四方遠近名士會者六七千人。

translations.literal: When the burial was to take place, renowned scholars from far and near assembled—six or seven thousand in number.
translations.idiomatic: As the burial approached, eminent scholars from near and far gathered—six or seven thousand in all.

sentences.zh: 初，瓊之教授於家。

translations.literal: Formerly, Qiong had taught scholars at his home.
translations.idiomatic: In earlier days Qiong had instructed students in his own household.

sentences.zh: 徐稚從之咨訪大義，及瓊貴，稚絕不復交。

translations.literal: Xu Zhi had followed him to inquire into the great principles; when Qiong rose to high rank, Zhi broke off all further contact.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhi had studied under him to seek instruction in the great principles, but once Qiong attained high office, Zhi ceased all further association.

sentences.zh: 至是，稚往吊之，進酹，哀哭而去，人莫知者。

translations.literal: At this time Zhi went to mourn him, advanced the libation, wept in grief, and departed—no one knew who he was.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhi came to mourn him, offered the libation, wept bitterly, and left—yet no one recognized him.

sentences.zh: 諸名士推問喪宰，宰曰：「先時有一書生來，衣粗薄而哭之哀，不記姓字。

translations.literal: The renowned scholars questioned the funeral steward. The steward said: "Earlier a scholar came, dressed in coarse thin garments and weeping bitterly—I do not recall his surname."
translations.idiomatic: The assembled scholars pressed the funeral steward for an account. He said, "A while ago a scholar came in coarse, thin clothing and wept with great sorrow—I do not remember his name."

sentences.zh: 」眾曰：「必徐孺子也。

translations.literal: The crowd said: "It must be Master Xu the Recluse."
translations.idiomatic: The company said, "That must be Xu Ruzi."

sentences.zh: 」於是選能言者陳留茅容輕騎追之，及於塗。

translations.literal: Thereupon they chose an eloquent man—Mao Rong of Chenliu—who rode swiftly in pursuit and caught up with him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: They then selected an articulate man, Mao Rong of Chenliu, who rode lightly in pursuit and overtook him on the road.

sentences.zh: 容為沽酒市肉，稚為飲食。

translations.literal: Rong bought wine and meat at market; Zhi ate and drank.
translations.idiomatic: Rong purchased wine and meat in town, and Zhi ate and drank with him.

sentences.zh: 容問國家之事，稚不答。

translations.literal: Rong asked about affairs of state; Zhi did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Rong asked about affairs of state, but Zhi would not reply.

sentences.zh: 更問稼穡之事，稚乃答之。

translations.literal: He then asked about farming; Zhi answered that.
translations.idiomatic: When he turned to questions of farming, Zhi answered those.

sentences.zh: 容還，以語諸人，或曰：「孔子云：『可與言而不與言，失人。

translations.literal: Rong returned and told the company. Someone said: "Confucius said: 'One who could be spoken with and is not spoken to—this is to lose a man.'"
translations.idiomatic: Rong returned and reported this to the others. Someone said, "Confucius said, 'To meet one with whom one may speak and not speak with him is to lose a man.'"

sentences.zh: 』然則孺子其失人乎？

translations.literal: "Then has the Recluse lost a man?"
translations.idiomatic: "Has Ruzi then lost a man?"

sentences.zh: 」太原郭泰曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Guo Tai of Taiyuan said: "Not so."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai of Taiyuan said, "Not at all."

sentences.zh: 孺子之為人，清潔高廉，饑不可得食，寒不可得衣，而為季偉飲酒食肉，此為已知季偉之賢故也。

translations.literal: "The Recluse's character is pure and lofty in integrity; when hungry he cannot get food, when cold he cannot get clothing—yet he drank and ate with Ji Wei. This was because he already knew Ji Wei's worth."
translations.idiomatic: "Ruzi is pure and lofty in integrity—when hungry he will not take food, when cold he will not take clothing—yet he drank and ate with Ji Wei because he already knew Ji Wei to be worthy."

sentences.zh: 所以不答國事者，是其智可及，其愚不可及也。

translations.literal: "The reason he did not answer on affairs of state is that one's wisdom may reach men, but one's folly may not."
translations.idiomatic: "The reason he would not discuss affairs of state is that his wisdom may be matched, but his folly cannot be fathomed."

sentences.zh: 泰博學，善談論。

translations.literal: Tai was broadly learned and skilled in discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai was broadly learned and excelled in discussion.

sentences.zh: 初游雒陽，時人莫識，陳留符融一見嗟異，因以介於河南尹李膺。

translations.literal: When he first traveled to Luoyang, no one of the time knew him. Fu Rong of Chenliu, at a single meeting, marvelled at him and introduced him to the Intendant of Henan, Li Ying.
translations.idiomatic: On his first visit to Luoyang none in the capital knew him, but Fu Rong of Chenliu, at a single meeting, was struck with wonder and introduced him to the Intendant of Henan, Li Ying.

sentences.zh: 膺與相見，曰：「吾見士多矣，未有如郭林宗者也。

translations.literal: Ying met with him and said: "I have seen many scholars, but none like Guo Linzong."
translations.idiomatic: Ying received him and said, "I have met many scholars, yet none like Guo Linzong."

sentences.zh: 其聰識通朗，高雅密博，今之華夏，鮮見其儔。

translations.literal: "His keen insight is penetrating and bright, his elegance refined and learned far and wide—among the civilized lands of today, few match his peer."
translations.idiomatic: "His keen intelligence is penetrating and luminous, his cultivation refined and profound—in all the civilized realm today, few can stand beside him."

sentences.zh: 」遂與為友，於是名震京師。

translations.literal: He thereupon became friends with him, and his fame shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon befriended him, and Tai's name resounded through the capital.

sentences.zh: 後歸鄉里，衣冠諸儒送至河上，車數千兩，膺唯與泰同舟而濟，眾賓望之，以為神仙焉。

translations.literal: Later he returned to his native district. Confucian gentry sent him off to the river—carriages numbered in the thousands. Ying alone boarded the same boat to cross with Tai; the guests looked upon them and thought them immortals.
translations.idiomatic: Later he returned home. Gentry and scholars escorted him to the river in thousands of carriages. Ying alone shared a boat with Tai to cross; the guests gazed upon them as though they were immortals.

sentences.zh: 泰性明知人，好獎訓士類，周遊郡國。

translations.literal: Tai by nature was clear-sighted in knowing men and loved to encourage and instruct the scholar class, traveling through the commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was by nature discerning in judging men and delighted in encouraging and guiding scholars, traveling through the commanderies.

sentences.zh: 茅容，年四十餘，耕於野，與等輩避雨樹下，眾皆夷踞相對，容獨危坐愈恭；

translations.literal: Mao Rong, over forty years of age, was plowing in the fields. He and companions took shelter from rain under a tree; all sprawled with legs spread facing one another, while Rong alone sat upright with ever greater respect;
translations.idiomatic: Mao Rong, past forty, was plowing in the fields. He and his companions sheltered from rain beneath a tree; the rest sat with legs sprawled facing one another, while Rong alone sat upright with growing decorum.

sentences.zh: 泰見而異之，因請寓宿。

translations.literal: Tai saw this and marvelled at him, and so asked to lodge the night.
translations.idiomatic: Tai noticed this, was struck with wonder, and asked to stay the night.

sentences.zh: 旦日，容殺雞為饌，泰謂為己設；

translations.literal: The next morning Rong killed a chicken for a meal. Tai thought it was prepared for himself;
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Rong killed a chicken for a meal, and Tai assumed it was meant for him;

sentences.zh: 容分半食母，餘半庋置，自以草蔬與客同飯。

translations.literal: Rong divided half to feed his mother, stored the other half away, and himself ate vegetables with his guest.
translations.idiomatic: Rong gave half to his mother, set the other half aside, and himself shared plain vegetables with his guest.

sentences.zh: 泰曰：「卿賢哉遠矣！

translations.literal: Tai said: "You are virtuous indeed—how far it reaches!
translations.idiomatic: Tai said, "You are virtuous indeed—how far that virtue extends!

sentences.zh: 郭林宗猶減三牲之具以供賓旅，而卿如此，乃我友也。

translations.literal: Even Guo Linzong would reduce the three sacrificial beasts to entertain traveling guests, yet you are like this—you are my friend."
translations.idiomatic: Even I would trim the three sacrificial animals to entertain guests, yet you act like this—you are my friend."

sentences.zh: 」起，對之揖，勸令從學，卒為盛德。

translations.literal: He rose, bowed to him in courtesy, urged him to follow him in study, and Rong ultimately became a man of great virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose, bowed to him, urged him to pursue learning, and Rong in the end became a man of eminent virtue.

sentences.zh: 巨鹿孟敏，客居太原，荷甑墮地，不顧而去。

translations.literal: Meng Min of Julu, lodging in Taiyuan, let a carrying pot fall to the ground and went off without looking back.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Min of Julu, while lodging in Taiyuan, dropped a carrying pot to the ground and walked on without a glance.

sentences.zh: 泰見而問其意，對曰：「甑已破矣，視之何益！

translations.literal: Tai saw this and asked his meaning. He replied: "The pot is already broken—what use is there in looking at it?"
translations.idiomatic: Tai saw this and asked what he meant. He replied, "The pot is already broken—what good is there in looking at it?"

sentences.zh: 」泰以為有分決，與之言，知其德性，因勸令遊學，遂知名當世。

translations.literal: Tai regarded him as having power of decision; he spoke with him, knew his moral character, and urged him to travel for study—he thus became famous in his age.
translations.idiomatic: Tai took this as proof of decisive character, spoke with him and perceived his moral quality, urged him to travel for study, and he thus won fame in his time.

sentences.zh: 陳留申屠蟠，家貧，傭為漆工；

translations.literal: Shen Tu Pan of Chenliu—his family was poor; he hired out as a lacquerer;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Tu Pan of Chenliu was poor and hired himself out as a lacquerer;

sentences.zh: 鄢陵庾乘，少給事縣廷為門士；

translations.literal: Yu Cheng of Yanling, in youth served in the county hall as a gate attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Yu Cheng of Yanling in his youth served in the county offices as a gate attendant;

sentences.zh: 泰見而奇之，其後皆為名士。

translations.literal: Tai saw them and marvelled at them; afterward both became renowned scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Tai noticed them and was struck with wonder; both later became celebrated scholars.

sentences.zh: 自餘或出於屠沽、卒伍，因泰獎進成名者甚眾。

translations.literal: Of the rest, some came from butchers and peddlers, soldiers and guards—through Tai's encouragement and advancement, many rose to fame.
translations.idiomatic: Among the others were men from butcher stalls and wine shops, from the ranks of soldiers and guards—through Tai's praise and promotion, very many came to renown.

sentences.zh: 陳國童子魏昭請於泰曰：「經師易遇，人師難遭，願在左右，供給灑掃。

translations.literal: Wei Zhao, a youth of Chen, requested of Tai: "Masters of the classics are easy to meet; a master of men is hard to encounter. I wish to remain at your side to supply sweeping and sprinkling."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhao, a youth of Chen state, asked Tai, "Teachers of the classics are easy to find, but a teacher of character is hard to meet. I wish to remain at your side and attend to sweeping and sprinkling."

sentences.zh: 」泰許之。

translations.literal: Tai assented.
translations.idiomatic: Tai agreed.

sentences.zh: 泰嘗不佳，命昭作粥，粥成，進泰，泰呵之曰：「為長者作粥，不加意敬，使不可食！

translations.literal: When Tai was unwell he ordered Zhao to make gruel. When the gruel was ready and Zhao presented it, Tai scolded him: "Making gruel for an elder without attentive respect—this makes it unfit to eat!"
translations.idiomatic: Once when Tai was indisposed he had Zhao cook gruel. When it was done and Zhao brought it in, Tai rebuked him: "To cook gruel for an elder without proper care—this is not fit to eat!"

sentences.zh: 」以杯擲地。

translations.literal: He threw the cup to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He hurled the cup to the floor.

sentences.zh: 昭更為粥重進，泰復呵之。

translations.literal: Zhao made gruel again and presented it anew; Tai scolded him again.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao cooked gruel again and presented it once more; Tai scolded him again.

sentences.zh: 如此者三，昭姿容無變。

translations.literal: This happened three times, yet Zhao's bearing did not change.
translations.idiomatic: This occurred three times, yet Zhao's demeanor never altered.

sentences.zh: 泰乃曰：「吾始見子之面，而今而後，知卿心耳！

translations.literal: Tai then said: "When I first saw your face, and only now—then I know your heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Tai then said, "I knew your face at first; only now do I know your heart!"

sentences.zh: 」遂友而善之。

translations.literal: He thereupon befriended him and treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon took him as a friend and treated him kindly.

sentences.zh: 陳留左原，為郡學生，犯法見斥，泰遇諸路，為設酒餚以慰之。

translations.literal: Zuo Yuan of Chenliu, a student of the commandery school, violated the law and was expelled. Tai met him on the road and set out wine and food to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Yuan of Chenliu, a student in the commandery school, broke the law and was dismissed. Tai encountered him on the road and laid out wine and food to console him.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「昔顏涿聚，梁甫之巨盜，段干木，晉國之大駔，卒為齊之忠臣，魏之名賢；

translations.literal: He said: "In former times Yan Zhuoju was a great bandit of Liangfu, and Duan Ganmu was a great bully of Jin—yet in the end one became a loyal minister of Qi, the other a famed worthy of Wei;
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Long ago Yan Zhuoju was a great robber of Liangfu and Duan Ganmu a great ruffian of Jin, yet in the end one became a loyal minister of Qi and the other a celebrated worthy of Wei;

sentences.zh: 蘧瑗、顏回尚不能無過，況其餘乎！

translations.literal: Qu Yuan and Yan Hui could not be without fault—how much more the rest!
translations.idiomatic: Qu Yuan and Yan Hui could not be without faults—how much more ordinary men!

sentences.zh: 慎勿恚恨，責躬而已！

translations.literal: "Take care not to harbor resentment—blame only yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: "Take care not to nurse resentment—examine yourself alone!"

sentences.zh: 」原納其言而去。

translations.literal: Yuan accepted his words and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan took his counsel and left.

sentences.zh: 或有譏泰不絕惡人者，泰曰：「人而不仁，疾之已甚，亂也。

translations.literal: Some criticized Tai for not cutting off wicked men. Tai said: "For a man who lacks benevolence, to hate him excessively is to bring disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Some reproached Tai for not breaking with wicked men altogether. Tai said, "When a man lacks benevolence, to hate him beyond measure is to invite disorder."

sentences.zh: 」原後忽更懷忿結客，欲報諸生，其日，泰在學，原愧負前言，因遂罷去。

translations.literal: "Yuan later suddenly harbored resentment again and gathered clients, intending to take revenge on the students. On that day Tai was at the school; Yuan, ashamed that he had failed his earlier words, thereupon abandoned the plan and left.
translations.idiomatic: "Yuan later again secretly nursed anger and gathered retainers, intending to strike back at the students. That day Tai was in the school; Yuan, ashamed before his earlier pledge, then gave up the plan and went away.

sentences.zh: 後事露，眾人鹹謝服焉。

translations.literal: When the affair later came to light, the company all thanked him and submitted in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter later came to light, everyone thanked Tai and acknowledged his foresight.

sentences.zh: 或問范滂曰：「郭林宗何如人？

translations.literal: Someone asked Fan Pang: "What sort of man is Guo Linzong?"
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Fan Pang, "What manner of man is Guo Linzong?"

sentences.zh: 」滂曰：「隱不違親，貞不絕俗，天子不得臣，諸侯不得友，吾不知其它。

translations.literal: Pang said: "In seclusion he does not betray his kin; in integrity he does not break with the world. The Son of Heaven cannot make him a subject; feudal lords cannot make him a friend—I know nothing beyond this."
translations.idiomatic: Pang said, "In retirement he does not forsake his kin; in uprightness he does not cut himself off from the world. The Son of Heaven cannot treat him as a subject; feudal lords cannot treat him as a mere friend—I know no more than this."

sentences.zh: 」泰嘗舉有道，不就，同郡宋沖素服其德，以為自漢元以來，未見其匹，嘗勸之仕。

translations.literal: Tai was once recommended as a man of manifest virtue but did not accept office. Song Chong of the same commandery, who had always admired his virtue, held that since the time of Emperor Yuan of Han none had matched him, and once urged him to take office.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was once nominated as a man of manifest virtue but would not take office. Song Chong of the same commandery, who had long revered his character, held that since Emperor Yuan none had been his equal, and once urged him to serve.

sentences.zh: 泰曰：「吾夜觀乾象，晝察人事，天之所廢，不可支也，吾將優遊卒歲而已。

translations.literal: Tai said: "By night I observe the heavenly signs; by day I examine human affairs. What Heaven has cast off cannot be propped up—I intend only to pass my remaining years at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Tai said, "By night I read the signs of Heaven; by day I observe human affairs. What Heaven has abandoned cannot be upheld—I mean only to spend my remaining years in ease."

sentences.zh: 」然猶周旋京師，誨誘不息。

translations.literal: Yet he still moved about the capital, instructing and guiding without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he still moved in the capital, teaching and exhorting without rest.

sentences.zh: 徐稚以書戒之曰：「夫大木將顛，非一繩所維，何為棲棲不遑寧處！

translations.literal: Xu Zhi admonished him in a letter: "The great tree is about to topple—not one rope can hold it. Why do you bustle about, never finding rest?"
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhi warned him in a letter: "The great tree is about to fall—not one rope can steady it. Why do you hurry to and fro, never at peace?"

sentences.zh: 」泰感寤曰：「謹拜斯言，以為師表。

translations.literal: Tai, moved, said: "I respectfully accept these words as my teacher's model."
translations.idiomatic: Tai, stirred, said, "I accept these words with reverence as the model of a teacher."

sentences.zh: 」濟陰黃允，以俊才知名，泰見而謂曰：「卿高才絕人，足成偉器，年過四十，聲名著矣。

translations.literal: Huang Yun of Jiyin was known for outstanding talent. Tai met him and said: "Your lofty gifts surpass other men and are enough to become a great vessel. You have passed forty and your fame is already established."
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yun of Jiyin was famed for exceptional talent. When Tai met him he said, "Your eminent gifts surpass others and are enough to make a great vessel of you. You have passed forty and your reputation is already secure."

sentences.zh: 然至於此際，當深自匡持，不然，將失之矣！

translations.literal: "Yet at this juncture you must deeply restrain yourself—otherwise you will lose what you have gained!"
translations.idiomatic: "Yet at this point you must hold yourself strictly in check—otherwise you will lose it all!"

sentences.zh: 」後司徒袁隗欲為從女求姻，見允，歎曰：「得婿如是，足矣。

translations.literal: Later the Excellency of Works Yuan Wei wished to arrange a marriage for a clanswoman and, meeting Yun, sighed: "To gain a son-in-law like this is enough."
translations.idiomatic: Later the Excellency of Works Yuan Wei wished to obtain a husband for a clanswoman. Meeting Yun, he sighed, "To gain a son-in-law like this is enough."

sentences.zh: 」允聞而黜遣其妻。

translations.literal: When Yun heard this he dismissed his wife.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun heard of it he sent his wife away.

sentences.zh: 妻請大會宗親為別，因於眾中攘袂數允隱慝十五事而去，允以此廢於時。

translations.literal: His wife asked for a great assembly of kin to take leave, and there before the crowd rolled up her sleeves and recounted fifteen hidden faults of Yun before departing. Yun was thereby ruined in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His wife asked to gather the clan for a farewell, then before them all rolled up her sleeves and listed fifteen secret failings of Yun before she left. Yun was thereby disgraced in his day.

sentences.zh: 初，允與漢中晉文經並恃其才智，曜名遠近，征辟不就。

translations.literal: Formerly Yun and Jin Wenjing of Hanzhong both relied on their talent and intelligence, dazzling fame far and near, and would not answer summons to office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yun and Jin Wenjing of Hanzhong had both trusted in their talent and wit, their renown dazzling near and far, and refused all summons to office.

sentences.zh: 託言療病京師，不通賓客，公卿大夫遺門生旦暮問疾，郎吏雜坐其門，猶不得見；

translations.literal: They claimed to be treating illness in the capital and would not receive guests. Grandees and high ministers sent students morning and evening to inquire after their health; clerks and attendants sat mixed at their gates—yet still they could not be seen;
translations.idiomatic: They pleaded illness in the capital and would not see guests. Grandees sent pupils morning and evening to ask after their health; clerks and attendants sat crowded at their gates—yet they still could not gain an audience;

sentences.zh: 三公所辟召者，輒以詢訪之，隨所臧否，以為與奪。

translations.literal: Whomever the Three Excellencies wished to recruit, they would consult these two; according to their praise or blame, appointments and dismissals were decided.
translations.idiomatic: Whomever the Three Excellencies meant to recruit, they would first consult these two; praise or blame from them determined appointment or rejection.

sentences.zh: 符融謂李膺曰：「二子行業無聞，以豪桀自置，遂使公卿問疾，王臣坐門，融恐其小道破義，空譽違實，特宜察焉。

translations.literal: Fu Rong said to Li Ying: "These two men have no reputation for conduct or achievement, yet set themselves up as heroes—so that grandees inquire after their health and royal ministers sit at their gates. I fear their petty ways may break righteousness and empty fame betray reality; they should especially be examined."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Rong said to Li Ying, "These two have no record of conduct or achievement, yet pose as heroes until grandees ask after their health and ministers sit at their gates. I fear their petty arts may rupture righteousness and hollow fame belie the fact—they ought especially to be scrutinized."

sentences.zh: 」膺然之。

translations.literal: Ying agreed with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ying assented.

sentences.zh: 二人自是名論漸衰，賓徒稍省，旬日之間，慚歎逃去，後並以罪廢棄。

translations.literal: The two men's reputations gradually declined; their followers dwindled. Within ten days they fled in shame and regret, and later both were disgraced and cast aside for crimes.
translations.idiomatic: The reputations of the two men gradually faded; their followers thinned. Within ten days they slunk away in shame, and later both were ruined by crime.

sentences.zh: 陳留仇香，至行純嘿，鄉黨無知者。

translations.literal: Qiu Xiang of Chenliu possessed the utmost conduct yet was pure and silent—his village neighbors did not know him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Xiang of Chenliu was of the highest integrity yet plain and reticent—his neighbors in the district did not know him.

sentences.zh: 年四十，為蒲亭長。

translations.literal: At forty he became chief of Pu District.
translations.idiomatic: At forty he became magistrate of Pu District.

sentences.zh: 民有陳元，獨與母居，母詣香告元不孝。

translations.literal: A man named Chen Yuan lived alone with his mother. The mother went to Xiang and accused Yuan of unfilial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Among the people was Chen Yuan, who lived alone with his mother. The mother came before Xiang and accused Yuan of lacking filial piety.

sentences.zh: 香驚曰：「吾近日過元捨，廬落整頓，耕耘以時，此非惡人，當是教化未至耳。

translations.literal: Xiang was startled and said: "I recently passed Yuan's dwelling—the homestead was in good order and he plowed on schedule. This is not a wicked man; instruction has simply not yet reached him."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang was astonished and said, "I passed Yuan's house not long ago—the compound was tidy and he farmed on time. This is no villain; teaching has simply not yet taken hold."

sentences.zh: 母守寡養孤，苦身投老，奈何以一旦之忿，棄歷年之勤乎！

translations.literal: "A mother who kept her widowhood to raise an orphan, who toiled her body and gave her old age—how can you, in a moment's anger, cast away years of labor?"
translations.idiomatic: "You kept widowhood to raise an orphan, wore yourself out and gave your old age—how can one burst of anger undo years of toil?"

sentences.zh: 且母養人遺孤，不能成濟，若死者有知，百歲之後，當何以見亡者！

translations.literal: "Moreover, in raising another man's orphaned child, if you cannot bring the task to completion, should the dead have consciousness—after a hundred years, how will you face the departed?"
translations.idiomatic: "And in raising another's orphan, if you cannot see it through, should the dead have awareness—after a hundred years, how will you face your husband?"

sentences.zh: 」母涕泣而起，香乃親到元家，為陳人倫孝行，譬以禍福之言，元感悟，卒為孝子。

translations.literal: The mother wept, rose, and departed. Xiang then went in person to Yuan's home, set forth for him the human bonds and filial conduct, and spoke to him with words of blessing and calamity. Yuan was moved to insight and in the end became a filial son.
translations.idiomatic: The mother wept, rose, and left. Xiang then went himself to Yuan's home, explained human relations and filial duty, and admonished him with words of fortune and ruin. Yuan was awakened and became a filial son in the end.

sentences.zh: 考城令河內王奐署香主簿，謂之曰：「聞在蒲亭，陳元不罰而化之，得無少鷹鸇之志邪？

translations.literal: Wang Huan, magistrate of Kaocheng in Henei, appointed Xiang chief clerk and said to him: "I heard that in Pu you did not punish Chen Yuan but transformed him—have you not a little of the hawk-and-falcon's spirit?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huan, magistrate of Kaocheng in Henei, made Xiang chief clerk and said, "I heard that in Pu you did not punish Chen Yuan but reformed him—surely you have something of the hawk and falcon in you?"

sentences.zh: 」香曰：「以為鷹鸇不若鸞鳳，故不為也。

translations.literal: Xiang said: "I hold that hawk and falcon are not the match of the phoenix—therefore I do not act as they do."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "I consider that hawk and falcon cannot compare with the phoenix—therefore I do not act like them."

sentences.zh: 」奐曰：「枳棘之林非鸞鳳所集，百里非大賢之路。

translations.literal: Huan said: "A forest of thorned citron is no nesting place for phoenixes; a hundred li is no road for a great worthy."
translations.idiomatic: Huan said, "A thorn-brake is no roost for a phoenix; a hundred li is no path for a great worthy."

sentences.zh: 」乃以一月奉資香，使入太學。

translations.literal: He thereupon gave Xiang one month's salary and sent him into the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave Xiang one month's salary and sent him to the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 郭泰、符融繼刺謁之，因留宿。

translations.literal: Guo Tai and Fu Rong successively called upon him and lodged the night.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Tai and Fu Rong called on him in turn and stayed overnight.

sentences.zh: 明旦，泰起，下床拜之曰：「君，泰之師，非泰之友也。

translations.literal: At dawn Tai rose, descended from the couch, and bowed to him, saying: "You, sir, are my teacher—not merely my friend."
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Tai rose, stepped down from the couch, and bowed to him, saying, "You, sir, are my teacher—not merely my friend."

sentences.zh: 」香學畢歸鄉里，雖在宴居，必正衣服，妻子事之若嚴君；

translations.literal: When Xiang finished his studies and returned home, even in leisurely repose he always wore proper dress; wife and children served him as though he were a stern lord;
translations.idiomatic: When Xiang completed his studies and returned home, even at leisure he always wore proper garments; wife and children served him as to a strict master;

sentences.zh: 妻子有過，免冠自責，妻子庭謝思過，香冠，妻子乃敢升堂，終不見其喜怒聲色之異。

translations.literal: When wife or children had faults, he removed his cap and blamed himself; wife and children would apologize in the courtyard for their errors, and only when Xiang put on his cap again would wife and children dare enter the hall. To the end one never saw change in his expression or tone of joy or anger.
translations.idiomatic: If wife or children erred, he took off his cap and reproached himself; they would apologize in the courtyard, and only when Xiang put on his cap again would they dare enter the hall. Never to the end did one see his face or voice alter with pleasure or anger.

sentences.zh: 不應徵辟，卒於家。

translations.literal: He did not answer summons to office and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He would not accept summons to office and died at home.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸亥，隕石於鄠。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day guihai, a meteorite fell at Hu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on guihai day, a meteorite fell at Hu.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，己丑，京師雨雹。

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, on the day jichou, hail fell in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fifth month, on jichou day, hail fell in the capital.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史度尚募諸蠻夷擊艾縣城，大破之，降者數萬人。

translations.literal: Du Shang, Inspector of Jing province, recruited various barbarian peoples to attack Aicheng and inflicted a great defeat; those who surrendered numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shang, Inspector of Jing province, recruited various tribal peoples to attack Aicheng, routed the enemy utterly, and received the surrender of tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 桂陽宿賊卜陽、潘鴻等逃入深山。

translations.literal: The long-established bandits of Guiyang, Bu Yang and Pan Hong, fled into the deep mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The veteran bandits of Guiyang, Bu Yang and Pan Hong, fled into the deep mountains.

sentences.zh: 尚窮追數百里，破其三屯，多獲珍寶。

translations.literal: Shang pursued them relentlessly for several hundred li, broke three of their encampments, and seized many treasures.
translations.idiomatic: Shang pursued them hard for several hundred li, destroyed three of their camps, and seized a great store of valuables.

sentences.zh: 陽、鴻黨眾猶盛，尚欲擊之，而士卒驕富，莫有鬥志。

translations.literal: The factions of Yang and Hong were still strong. Shang wished to attack further, but the soldiers had grown arrogant and wealthy and none had fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Yang and Hong still had a large following. Shang wished to press the attack, but his troops had grown proud and rich and none would fight.

sentences.zh: 尚計緩之則不戰，逼之必逃亡，乃宣言：「卜陽、潘鴻作賊十年，習於攻守，今兵寡少，未易可進，當須諸郡所發悉至，乃並力攻之。

translations.literal: Shang calculated that if he moved slowly they would not fight, but if pressed they would surely flee. He therefore proclaimed: "Bu Yang and Pan Hong have been bandits for ten years and are skilled in attack and defense. Our forces are few and it will not be easy to advance—we must wait until all the troops raised by the various commanderies have arrived, and then strike together."
translations.idiomatic: Shang reasoned that if he moved slowly they would not give battle, but if driven hard they would surely escape. He therefore announced, "Bu Yang and Pan Hong have been bandits for ten years and know how to attack and defend. Our numbers are few and an advance would not be easy—we must wait until every detachment raised by the commanderies has arrived, then strike with combined force."

sentences.zh: 」申令軍中恣聽射獵，兵士喜悅，大小皆出。

translations.literal: He then ordered the army to hunt at will. The soldiers were delighted and all went out, great and small alike.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave orders that the army might hunt freely. The soldiers were delighted and all went out, officers and men alike.

sentences.zh: 尚乃密使所親客潛焚其營，珍積皆盡。

translations.literal: Shang then secretly sent a trusted retainer to burn their camp in secret—all stores of treasure were consumed.
translations.idiomatic: Shang then secretly had a trusted follower set fire to their camp—all their hoarded goods were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 獵者來還，莫不潤涕。

translations.literal: When the hunters returned, none failed to weep profusely.
translations.idiomatic: When the hunters returned, every man wept bitterly.

sentences.zh: 尚人人慰勞，深自咎責，因曰：「卜陽等財寶足富數世，諸卿但不並力耳，所亡少少，何足介意！

translations.literal: Shang consoled every man and deeply blamed himself, then said: "The treasure of Bu Yang and the rest is enough to enrich them for generations—you gentlemen simply did not exert yourselves together. What was lost is but little—why take it to heart!"
translations.idiomatic: Shang comforted each man and took the blame upon himself, then said, "Bu Yang and the others have hoarded enough wealth to enrich their families for generations—you only failed to act together. What we lost is trifling—why dwell on it!"

sentences.zh: 」眾鹹憤踴。

translations.literal: The crowd all burned with indignation and leapt to action.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were stirred to fury and eager for battle.

sentences.zh: 尚敕令秣馬蓐食，明旦，逕赴賊屯，陽、鴻等自以深固，不復設備，吏士乘銳，遂破平之。

translations.literal: Shang ordered them to feed their horses and take bed-meal; at dawn he went straight to the bandits' camp. Yang, Hong, and the rest, trusting in their deep stronghold, made no further preparations. The officers and soldiers, riding their keen edge, thereupon broke and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Shang ordered the men to feed their horses and take a meal before sleep; at dawn he marched straight on the rebels' camp. Yang and Hong, trusting their mountain fastness, relaxed their guard. The officers and soldiers, fierce in attack, routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 尚出兵三年，群寇悉定，封右鄉侯。

translations.literal: Shang had campaigned for three years; all the bandit groups were pacified, and he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Youxiang.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in the field Shang had pacified every band, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Youxiang.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬寅，帝南巡；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day renyin, the Emperor made a southern tour;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on renyin day, the Emperor toured south;

sentences.zh: 庚申，幸章陵；

translations.literal: On the day gengshen he visited Zhangling;
translations.idiomatic: on gengshen day he visited Zhangling;

sentences.zh: 戊辰，幸雲夢，臨漢水，還，幸新野。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen he visited Yunmeng, came to the Han River, returned, and visited Xinye.
translations.idiomatic: on wuchen day he visited Yunmeng, went to the Han River, then returned and visited Xinye.

sentences.zh: 時公卿、貴戚車騎萬計，徵求費役，不可勝極。

translations.literal: At that time the grandees and noble kin had carriages and horsemen numbering in the tens of thousands; exactions and corvée costs were beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: At that time grandees and imperial kin turned out carriages and riders by the ten thousand; levies and labor costs were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 護駕從事桂陽胡騰上言：「天子無外，乘輿所幸，即為京師。

translations.literal: Hu Teng of Guiyang, an attendant on the imperial progress, submitted a memorial: "The Son of Heaven has no outside—wherever the imperial carriage favors, that is the capital."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Teng of Guiyang, an attendant on the progress, memorialized: "The Son of Heaven knows no exterior—wherever the imperial carriage alights, that place is the capital."

sentences.zh: 臣請以荊州刺史比司隸校尉，臣自同都官從事。

translations.literal: I ask that the Inspector of Jing be compared to the Director of the Retainers, and that I myself be compared to the Director of the Capital Offices."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Inspector of Jing be given powers like the Director of the Retainers, and that I be ranked with the Director of the Capital Offices."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 自是肅然，莫敢妄干擾郡縣。

translations.literal: From this the court grew stern; none dared rashly harass the commanderies and districts.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter discipline was restored and none dared meddle with the local administrations.

sentences.zh: 帝在南陽，左右並通姦利，詔書多除人為郎，太尉楊秉上疏曰：「太微積星，名為郎位，入奉宿衛，出牧百姓，宜割不忍之恩，以斷求欲之路。

translations.literal: While the Emperor was at Nanyang, those about him all trafficked in illicit profit; edicts frequently appointed men as palace attendants. Yang Bing, the Grand Commandant, submitted a memorial: "The accumulated stars of the Supreme Palace Enclosure are called the Officers' Seats—entering they serve in the guard, going forth they shepherd the people. It is fitting to cut off indulgent favor and block the road of covetous seeking."
translations.idiomatic: At Nanyang the Emperor's attendants all traded in illicit gain, and edicts frequently named men as palace gentlemen. Grand Commandant Yang Bing memorialized: "The clustered stars of the Supreme Palace Enclosure are called the Officers' Seats—within they guard the palace, without they govern the people. Your Majesty should cut indulgent favor and close the path of greedy petition."

sentences.zh: 」於是詔除乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon appointments by edict ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts appointing such men then ceased.

sentences.zh: 護羌校尉段熲擊當煎羌，破之。

translations.literal: Duan Jiong, Protector of the Qiang, attacked the Dangjian Qiang and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jiong, Protector of the Qiang, attacked the Dangjian Qiang and routed them.

sentences.zh: 十二月，辛丑，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day xinchou, the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on xinchou day, the Emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 中常侍汝陽侯唐衡、武原侯徐璜皆卒。

translations.literal: The Regular Attendants Tang Heng, Marquis of Ruyang, and Xu Huang, Marquis of Wuyuan, both died.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Tang Heng, Marquis of Ruyang, and Xu Huang, Marquis of Wuyuan, both died.

sentences.zh: 初，侍中寇榮，恂之曾孫也，性矜潔，少所與，以此為權寵所疾。

translations.literal: Formerly, Palace Attendant Kou Rong was a great-grandson of Kou Xun. By nature he was proud and fastidious and had few intimates; for this he was resented by those in power and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Palace Attendant Kou Rong was a great-grandson of Kou Xun. Proud and exacting by nature, he kept few companions, and for this the powerful and favored resented him.

sentences.zh: 榮從兄子尚帝妹益陽長公主，帝又納其從孫女於後宮。

translations.literal: Rong's clansman's son had married the Emperor's younger sister, the Princess of Yiyang; the Emperor had also taken Rong's grand-niece into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: A son of Rong's cousin had married the Emperor's sister, Princess of Yiyang; the Emperor had also taken Rong's grand-niece into the harem.

sentences.zh: 左右益忌之，遂共陷以罪，與宗族免歸故郡，吏承望風旨，持之浸急。

translations.literal: Those about the throne grew ever more jealous, and together framed him in a crime. He and his clan were dismissed and sent home to their native commandery; officials, reading the prevailing wind, pressed him ever harder.
translations.idiomatic: The courtiers grew more envious still and joined in framing him. He and his clan were stripped of office and sent to their home commandery, where officials, catching the court's mood, hounded him ever harder.

sentences.zh: 榮恐不免，詣闕自論。

translations.literal: Rong feared he could not escape and went to the capital to plead his case.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he could not escape, Rong went to court to plead his own cause.

sentences.zh: 未至，刺史張敬追劾榮以擅去邊，有詔捕之。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, the Inspector Zhang Jing pursued and impeached Rong for leaving his district without leave; an edict was issued to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived, Inspector Zhang Jing impeached him for leaving his district without authorization, and an edict ordered his arrest.

sentences.zh: 榮逃竄數年，會赦，不得除，積窮困，乃自亡命中上書曰：「陛下統天理物，作民父母，自生齒以上，鹹蒙德澤；

translations.literal: Rong fled and hid for several years. An amnesty came, yet he was not cleared. Reduced to utter want, he sent up a memorial from hiding: "Your Majesty governs Heaven and orders the myriad things, acting as parent to the people—from those who first cut their teeth upward, all have received your gracious favor;
translations.idiomatic: Rong fled and hid for years. An amnesty came, yet he was not pardoned. Driven to extremity, he sent a memorial from hiding: "Your Majesty governs Heaven and orders all things, the parent of the people—from the first cutting of teeth upward, all have bathed in your grace;

sentences.zh: 而臣兄弟獨以無辜，為專權之臣所見批抵，青蠅之人所共構會，令陛下忽慈母之仁，發投杼之怒。

translations.literal: yet my brothers alone, without guilt, have been struck down by ministers who monopolize power and slandered by men like flies on the wall, until Your Majesty has set aside a mother's kindness and unleashed the anger of a father who casts away his shuttle."
translations.idiomatic: yet my brothers alone, though innocent, have been struck by power-holding ministers and slandered by whisperers until Your Majesty has forsaken a mother's kindness and loosed a father's unjust rage."

sentences.zh: 殘諂之吏，張設機網，並驅爭先，若赴仇敵，罰及死沒，髡剔墳墓，欲使嚴朝必加濫罰；

translations.literal: Cruel and fawning officials have spread nets and snares; driving one another in rivalry as though rushing upon a foe, punishment reaches the dead, tombs are shaved and plundered—they would have the stern court heap excessive penalties;
translations.idiomatic: Cruel, fawning officials have spread nets and traps; racing one another as at a feud, punishment reaches the dead and tombs are defaced—they would make the stern court heap excessive penalties;

sentences.zh: 是以不敢觸突天威而自竄山林，以俟陛下發神聖之聽，啟獨睹之明，救可濟之人，援沒溺之命。

translations.literal: therefore I dared not offend Heaven's majesty and hid myself in the mountains and forests, waiting for Your Majesty to open your sacred hearing, awaken your solitary insight, save men who may yet be saved, and rescue lives drowning in peril."
translations.idiomatic: therefore I dared not offend Heaven's majesty and hid in the hills, waiting for Your Majesty to open sacred hearing, awaken singular insight, save those who may yet be saved, and rescue the drowning."

sentences.zh: 不意滯怒不為春夏息，淹恚不為歲時怠，遂馳使郵驛，佈告遠近，嚴文克剝，痛於霜雪，遂臣者窮人途，追臣者極車軌。

translations.literal: I did not expect that lingering anger would not rest in spring and summer, nor that deep resentment would not slacken with the seasons—messengers were dispatched by post, proclamations sent far and near, harsh words carved and cut, bitter as frost and snow. Those who submitted were driven to dead ends; those who pursued me filled the roads."
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect lingering wrath to know no spring or summer pause, nor deep resentment to ease with the year—couriers flew by post, notices went far and near, harsh words cut like frost and snow. Those who yielded were driven to ruin; pursuers filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 雖楚購伍員，漢求季布，無以過也。

translations.literal: Though Chu offered a price for Wu Zixu and Han sought Ji Bu, this could not surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: Though Chu hunted Wu Zixu and Han sought Ji Bu, nothing could match this.

sentences.zh: 臣遇罰以來，三赦再贖，無驗之罪，足以蠲除；

translations.literal: Since I met punishment, there have been three amnesties and two redemptions—crimes without proof enough to wipe them away;
translations.idiomatic: Since my punishment there have been three amnesties and two redemptions—unproven charges enough to clear me;

sentences.zh: 而陛下疾臣愈深，有司咎臣甫力，止則見掃滅，行則為亡虜，苟生則為窮人，極死則為冤鬼，天廣而無以自覆，地厚而無以自載，蹈陸土而有沉淪之憂，遠巖牆而有鎮壓之患。

translations.literal: yet Your Majesty's hostility toward me grows deeper. The authorities blame me for slight effort—if I stop I am swept away, if I move I am a fugitive; if I live I am a pauper, if I die utterly I am a wronged ghost. Heaven is wide yet I have no cover; earth is thick yet I have no support. Treading dry land I still fear sinking; far from the cliff wall I still fear being crushed."
translations.idiomatic: yet Your Majesty's hostility deepens. Officials blame my faint effort—if I stay I am destroyed, if I flee I am an outlaw; alive I am a beggar, dead I am a wronged ghost. Heaven is vast yet I cannot hide under it; earth is deep yet I cannot stand on it. On dry land I fear sinking; far from the wall I fear being crushed.

sentences.zh: 如臣犯元惡大憝，足以陳原野，備刀鋸，陛下當班布臣之所坐，以解眾論之疑。

translations.literal: If I have committed the greatest evil and chief crime, enough to be displayed in the open field and prepared for axe and saw, Your Majesty should publish my offenses to resolve the doubts of the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: If I have committed capital crime enough to be exposed in the open and meet axe and saw, let Your Majesty publish my offenses and resolve public doubt.

sentences.zh: 臣思入國門，坐於肺石之上，使三槐九棘平臣之罪，而閶闔九重，陷阱步設，舉趾觸罘罝，動行絓羅網，無緣至萬乘之前，永無見信之期。

translations.literal: I wish to enter the state gate and sit upon the lung stone, that the three huai and nine jing may judge my crime—yet the ninefold gates are trap and pit, every step touches the snare, every move catches in the net, with no path to the presence of ten thousand chariots and never a season of trust."
translations.idiomatic: I would enter the gate and sit on the red stone that the three huai and nine thorns might judge me—yet the ninefold gate is pit and trap, every step snares, every move entangles, with no path to ten thousand chariots and no season of trust.

sentences.zh: 悲夫，久生亦復何聊！

translations.literal: Alas—long life too brings what comfort!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—what comfort is there even in long life!

sentences.zh: 蓋忠臣殺身以解君怒，孝子殞命以寧親怨，故大舜不避塗廩、浚井之難，申生不辭姬氏讒邪之謗；

translations.literal: A loyal minister gives his body to appease his lord's anger; a filial son yields his life to quiet a parent's resentment. Thus Great Shun did not shun the hardships of the granary and the well; Shensheng did not refuse the slanders of the Ji clan."
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers die to appease their lord's wrath; filial sons perish to quiet a parent's resentment. Great Shun did not flee the granary and the well; Shensheng did not refuse the Ji clan's slanders.

sentences.zh: 臣敢忘斯義，不自斃以解明朝之忿哉！

translations.literal: How could I forget this principle and not destroy myself to resolve the court's wrath!"
translations.idiomatic: How could I forget this and not offer my life to resolve the court's wrath!"

sentences.zh: 乞以身塞責，願陛下丐亡兄弟死命，使臣一門頗有遺類，以崇陛下寬饒之惠。

translations.literal: I beg to use my body to answer the charge and ask Your Majesty to spare my brothers' lives, that my house may retain some remnant and Your Majesty's clement bounty be magnified."
translations.idiomatic: I beg to answer with my body and ask Your Majesty to spare my brothers, that our line may retain some remnant and Your Majesty's mercy be shown.

sentences.zh: 先死陳情，臨章泣血！

translations.literal: Before death I state my case; facing the memorial I weep blood!"
translations.idiomatic: Before death I lay bare my heart; writing this memorial I weep blood!

sentences.zh: 」帝省章愈怒，遂誅榮，寇氏由是衰廢。

translations.literal: When the Emperor read the memorial his anger only grew; he thereupon executed Rong, and the Kou clan from this declined and was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor read the memorial and grew only angrier; Rong was executed, and the Kou clan fell into ruin.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，帝遣中常侍左心官之苦縣祠老子。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, the Emperor sent the Regular Attendant Zuo Xin to sacrifice to Laozi at Ku County.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, the Emperor sent the eunuch Zuo Xin to offer sacrifice to Laozi at Ku County.

sentences.zh: 勃海王悝，素行險僻，多僭傲不法。

translations.literal: Liu Kui, King of Bohai, had always been devious and perverse, with many presumptuous and unlawful acts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kui, King of Bohai, had long been devious and lawless, full of presumptuous conduct.

sentences.zh: 北軍中候陳留史弼上封事曰：「臣聞帝王之於親戚，愛雖隆必示之以威，體雖貴必禁之以度，如是，和睦之道興，骨肉之恩遂矣。

translations.literal: Shi Bi of Chenliu, Director of the Northern Army, submitted a sealed memorial: "I have heard that emperors toward their kin, though love is deep must display authority, though status is noble must restrain with measure—if so, the way of harmony rises and the bond of flesh and blood is secured."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bi of Chenliu, Director of the Northern Army, submitted a sealed memorial: "Emperors toward kin, though love runs deep, must show authority; though rank is high, must bound with measure—then harmony thrives and flesh-and-blood bonds hold."

sentences.zh: 竊聞勃海王悝，外聚剽輕不逞之徒，內荒酒樂，出入無常，所與群居，皆家之棄子，朝之斥臣，必有羊勝、伍被之變。

translations.literal: I hear that King Kui of Bohai gathers violent and lawless men without, wastes himself in wine and music within, comes and goes without rule, and those with whom he consorts are all the cast-off sons of families and expelled ministers of court—surely there will be a calamity like Yang Sheng and Wu Bei."
translations.idiomatic: I hear King Kui of Bohai gathers ruffians without, drowns in wine and music within, comes and goes at whim, and his companions are cast-off sons and expelled ministers—surely a Yang Sheng or Wu Bei calamity awaits."

sentences.zh: 州司不敢彈糾，傅相不能匡輔，陛下隆於友於，不忍遏絕，恐遂滋蔓，為害彌大。

translations.literal: The provincial and commandery authorities dare not impeach; tutors and ministers cannot correct him. Your Majesty, extending brotherly affection, cannot bear to stop him—I fear the evil will spread and the harm grow greater."
translations.idiomatic: Provincial officials dare not impeach; tutors cannot correct him. Your Majesty, in brotherly affection, cannot bear to restrain him—I fear the evil will spread and harm grow.

sentences.zh: 乞露臣奏，宣示百僚，平處其法。

translations.literal: I beg that my memorial be displayed to the hundred officials and the law be applied impartially.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that this memorial be shown the hundred officials and the law applied fairly.

sentences.zh: 法決罪定，乃下不忍之詔；

translations.literal: Once the law has decided the crime, then issue an edict of clemency;
translations.idiomatic: Once guilt is fixed by law, then issue an edict of mercy;

sentences.zh: 臣下固執，然後少有所許。

translations.literal: your ministers below will press firmly, and then you may grant a little.
translations.idiomatic: your ministers will press firmly, and then you may grant a little relief.

sentences.zh: 如是，則聖朝無傷親之譏，勃海有享國之慶。

translations.literal: If so, the sacred court will have no reproach of harming kin, and Bohai will have the blessing of keeping its state."
translations.idiomatic: Then the court will not be charged with harming kin, and Bohai will keep its kingdom."

sentences.zh: 不然，懼大獄將興矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise, I fear a great trial will arise."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I fear a great trial will come."

sentences.zh: 」上不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 悝果謀為不道；

translations.literal: Kui indeed plotted sedition;
translations.idiomatic: Kui did plot treason;

sentences.zh: 有司請廢之，詔貶為癭陶王，食一縣。

translations.literal: the authorities requested his deposition. An edict demoted him to King of Yingtao, with sustenance from one district.
translations.idiomatic: authorities sought his removal. An edict demoted him to King of Yingtao with revenue from one district.

sentences.zh: 丙申晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: On the last day of the month bingchen there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the month, bingchen day, there was an eclipse of the sun.

sentences.zh: 詔公、卿、校尉舉賢良方正。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Excellencies, ministers, and colonels to recommend men of manifest virtue and upright character.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered excellencies, ministers, and colonels to recommend worthy men of manifest virtue and upright character.

sentences.zh: 千秋萬歲殿火。

translations.literal: The Hall of Ten Thousand Years burned.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Ten Thousand Years caught fire.

sentences.zh: 中常侍侯覽兄參為益州刺史，殘暴貪婪，累臧億計。

translations.literal: Hou Can, elder brother of the Regular Attendant Hou Lan, was Inspector of Yi province—cruel, violent, greedy, and corrupt, with accumulations of hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Can, elder brother of the eunuch Hou Lan, was Inspector of Yi province—cruel, violent, greedy, and corrupt, amassing hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 太尉楊秉奏檻車征參，參於道自殺，閱其車重三百餘兩，皆金銀錦帛。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yang Bing memorialized that he be brought in a caged cart. Can killed himself on the road; when his carriage was searched it weighed more than three hundred cart-loads, all gold, silver, and brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Yang Bing memorialized that he be brought in a prisoner's cart. Can killed himself on the road; his baggage weighed more than three hundred cart-loads of gold, silver, and silk.

sentences.zh: 秉因奏曰：「臣案舊典，宦官本在給使省闥，司昏守夜；

translations.literal: Bing further memorialized: "I examine the old statutes: eunuchs were originally for service within the gates, keeping watch at dusk and guarding through the night;
translations.idiomatic: Bing further wrote: "By old statute eunuchs served within the gates, keeping dusk watch and night guard;

sentences.zh: 而今猥受過寵，執政操權，附會者因公褒舉，違忤者求事中傷，居法王公，富擬國家，飲食極餚膳，僕妾盈紈素。

translations.literal: now they have received excessive favor, hold government and wield power; those who attach to them are praised and promoted on public business, those who oppose them are pursued and struck down in secret. They rank with kings and dukes, wealth rivals the state, food is the finest delicacies, servants and concubines fill rooms with silk."
translations.idiomatic: now they are over-favored, hold power and rule; followers are promoted on public business, opponents are destroyed in secret. They rank with kings, wealth rivals the state, tables overflow with delicacies, servants and concubines fill chambers of silk."

sentences.zh: 中常侍侯覽弟參，貪殘元惡，自取禍滅。

translations.literal: Hou Can, younger brother of the Regular Attendant Hou Lan, was greedy and cruel, the chief of evils, and brought destruction on himself."
translations.idiomatic: Hou Can, younger brother of the eunuch Hou Lan, was greedy and cruel, a chief of evils, and brought ruin on himself."

sentences.zh: 覽顧知釁重，必有自疑之意，臣愚以為不宜復見親近。

translations.literal: Lan, seeing the gravity of the offense, must harbor self-doubt—I humbly hold that he should not again be received in close attendance."
translations.idiomatic: Lan, knowing the gravity of the crime, must doubt himself—I hold he should no longer attend the throne closely."

sentences.zh: 昔懿公刑邴蜀阜之父，奪閻職之妻，而使二人參乘，卒有竹中之難。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Yi of Wei punished the fathers of Bing Shu and Yan Zhi, seized Yan Zhi's wife, and made the two men ride in his carriage—he ended with the disaster in the bamboo grove."
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Duke Yi of Wei punished the fathers of Bing Shu and Yan Zhi, seized Yan Zhi's wife, and made both ride beside him—he met disaster in the bamboo grove."

sentences.zh: 覽宜急屏斥，投畀有虎，若斯之人，非恩所宥，請免官送歸本郡。

translations.literal: Lan should quickly be removed and cast to where there are tigers; men like this are not to be spared by grace—I ask that he be dismissed from office and sent home to his native commandery."
translations.idiomatic: Lan should quickly be cast out to tiger country; such men are beyond grace—I ask that he be dismissed and sent to his home commandery."

sentences.zh: 」書奏，尚書召對秉掾屬，詰之曰：「設官分職，各有司存。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Masters of Writing summoned Bing's staff to question them: "Offices are established and duties divided—each has its charge."
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the Masters of Writing summoned Bing's staff and challenged them: "Offices are divided—each has its charge."

sentences.zh: 三公統外，御史察內。

translations.literal: The Three Excellencies govern the outer realm; the Imperial Secretary inspects the inner."
translations.idiomatic: The Three Excellencies govern without; the Imperial Secretary inspects within.

sentences.zh: 今越奏近官，經典、漢制，何所依據？

translations.literal: Now you overstep and memorialize on near officials—on what do the classics and Han institutions rely?"
translations.idiomatic: Now you overstep to impeach palace officials—what classic or Han statute supports this?

sentences.zh: 其開公具對！

translations.literal: Let the Excellency answer in full!"
translations.idiomatic: Let the Excellency answer fully!"

sentences.zh: 」秉使對曰：「《春秋傳》曰：『除君之惡，唯力是視。

translations.literal: Bing had his reply: "The Zuo Commentary says: 'Remove the ruler's evil—only strength is to be regarded.'"
translations.idiomatic: Bing had them answer: "The Zuo Commentary says, 'Remove the ruler's evil—only exert your strength.'"

sentences.zh: 』鄧通懈慢，申屠嘉召通詰責，文帝從而請之。

translations.literal: Deng Tong was negligent; Shen Tu Jia summoned and rebuked him, and Emperor Wen followed by pardoning him."
translations.idiomatic: Deng Tong was negligent; Shen Tu Jia summoned and rebuked him, and Emperor Wen pardoned him at Jia's request.

sentences.zh: 漢世故事，三公之職，無所不統。

translations.literal: By Han precedent the duties of the Three Excellencies embraced all things."
translations.idiomatic: By Han precedent the Three Excellencies oversaw all affairs.

sentences.zh: 尚書不能詰，帝不得已，竟免覽官。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing could not refute him; the Emperor, having no choice, at last dismissed Lan from office.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing could not rebut him; the Emperor, unwillingly, at last dismissed Lan.

sentences.zh: 司隸校尉韓縯因奏左悺罪惡，及其兄太僕南鄉侯稱請托州郡，聚斂為奸，賓客放縱，侵犯吏民。

translations.literal: Han Yan, Director of the Retainers, thereupon memorialized the crimes of Zuo Guan and his elder brother, the Grand Steward, Marquis of Nanxiang, Cheng, who had used influence with commanderies and districts and amassed wealth through corruption; their clients ran wild and encroached on officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Retainers Han Yan then memorialized the crimes of Zuo Guan and his elder brother Cheng, Grand Steward and Marquis of Nanxiang, who had peddled influence in the provinces and amassed wealth by corruption; their clients ran wild and oppressed officials and people.

sentences.zh: 悺、稱皆自殺。

translations.literal: Guan and Cheng both killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Guan and Cheng both committed suicide.

sentences.zh: 又奏中常侍具瑗兄沛相恭臧罪，征詣廷尉。

translations.literal: He also memorialized the corruption of Ju Yan's elder brother, the Chancellor of Pei, Gong, and Gong was summoned to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized the corruption of Ju Yan's elder brother Gong, Chancellor of Pei; Gong was summoned to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 瑗詣獄謝，上還東武侯印綬，詔貶為都鄉侯。

translations.literal: Yan went to the prison to apologize; the Emperor returned his seal and ribbon as Marquis of Dongwu and an edict demoted him to Marquis of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: Yan went to prison to apologize; the Emperor returned his Marquis of Dongwu seal and demoted him to Marquis of the Capital District.

sentences.zh: 超及璜、衡襲封者，並降為鄉侯，子弟分封者，悉奪爵土。

translations.literal: Chao, Huang, and Heng, who had inherited enfeoffments, were all demoted to district marquises; younger brothers and sons who had received separate enfeoffments all had their fiefs and lands stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Chao, Huang, and Heng, who had inherited marquisates, were all demoted to district marquises; younger brothers and sons with separate fiefs lost their lands.

sentences.zh: 劉普等貶為關內侯，尹勳等亦皆奪爵。

translations.literal: Liu Pu and the rest were demoted to marquises within the passes; Yin Xun and the others also lost their nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pu and others were demoted to marquises within the passes; Yin Xun and others also lost their ranks.

sentences.zh: 帝多內寵，宮女至五六千人，及驅役從使復兼倍於此，而鄧後恃尊驕忌，與帝所幸郭貴人更相譖訴。

translations.literal: The Emperor had many favorites within the palace; palace women reached five or six thousand, and corvée servants and attendants were again twice as many. Empress Dowager Deng, relying on her honored status, was proud and jealous and exchanged slanders with the Emperor's favorite, Lady Guo.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor kept many inner favorites; palace women reached five or six thousand, and corvée attendants doubled that again. Empress Dowager Deng, proud in her eminence, quarreled with the favored Lady Guo in mutual slander.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，廢皇后鄧氏，送暴室，以憂死。

translations.literal: On the day guihai the Empress Dowager Deng was deposed, sent to the Dank Chamber, and died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day Empress Deng was deposed, sent to the Dank Chamber, and died of grief.

sentences.zh: 河南尹鄧萬世、虎賁中郎將鄧會皆下獄誅。

translations.literal: Deng Wanshi, Intendant of Henan, and Deng Hui, Captain of the Tiger Guards, were both imprisoned and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Wanshi, Intendant of Henan, and Deng Hui, Captain of the Tiger Guards, were imprisoned and executed.

sentences.zh: 護羌校尉段熲擊罕姐羌，破之。

translations.literal: Duan Jiong, Protector of the Qiang, attacked the Hanjie Qiang and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jiong, Protector of the Qiang, attacked the Hanjie Qiang and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛巳，赦天下。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day xinsi, there was an amnesty for all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinsi day, an amnesty was proclaimed for the empire.

sentences.zh: 宛陵大姓羊元群罷北海郡，臧污狼籍；

translations.literal: Yang Yuanqun, a great clan of Wancheng, left office as Administrator of Beihai with corruption spread in every record;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuanqun of the great Wancheng clan left office as Administrator of Beihai with corruption notorious in every record;

sentences.zh: 郡捨溷軒有奇巧，亦載之以歸。

translations.literal: even ingenious fittings from the privy in the prefectural quarters were loaded and taken home.
translations.idiomatic: even clever fittings from the privy in the prefectural quarters were carted home.

sentences.zh: 河南尹李膺表按其罪；

translations.literal: Li Ying, Intendant of Henan, memorialized a table to investigate his crimes;
translations.idiomatic: Li Ying, Intendant of Henan, memorialized to investigate his crimes;

sentences.zh: 元群行賂宦官，膺竟反坐。

translations.literal: Yuanqun bribed the eunuchs, and Ying in the end was punished in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqun bribed the eunuchs, and Ying was punished in turn.

sentences.zh: 單超弟遷為山陽太守，以罪繫獄，廷尉馮緄考致其死；

translations.literal: Dan Chao's younger brother Qian was Administrator of Shanyang; imprisoned for a crime, the Minister of Justice Feng Gun examined him to death;
translations.idiomatic: Dan Chao's younger brother Qian was Administrator of Shanyang; imprisoned for crime, Minister of Justice Feng Gun's examination brought him to death;

sentences.zh: 中官相黨，共飛章誣緄以罪。

translations.literal: the palace officials banded together and jointly sent a flying memorial to slander Gun with crimes.
translations.idiomatic: palace officials banded together and sent flying memorials to slander Gun.

sentences.zh: 中常侍蘇康、管霸，固天下良田美業，州郡不敢詰，大司農劉祐移書所在，依科品沒入之；

translations.literal: The Regular Attendants Su Kang and Guan Ba had seized good fields and fine estates throughout the empire; commanderies and districts dared not investigate. Grand Minister of Agriculture Liu You sent letters to the locales to confiscate them according to statute;
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs Su Kang and Guan Ba had seized good fields and fine estates empire-wide; provinces dared not investigate. Grand Minister of Agriculture Liu You ordered confiscation by statute;

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，與膺、緄俱輸作左校。

translations.literal: the Emperor was greatly angered, and together with Ying and Gun they were sent to labor in the Left Construction Corps.
translations.idiomatic: the Emperor was furious, and Ying and Gun with him were sent to labor in the Left Construction Corps.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲寅，安陵園寢火。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day jiayin, the dormitory of the Anling mausoleum burned.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, on jiayin day, the dormitory of the Anling mausoleum burned.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，詔壞郡國諸淫祀，特留雒陽王渙、密縣卓茂二祠。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi an edict ordered the destruction of licentious shrines in commanderies and kingdoms, keeping only the shrines of King Huan of Luoyang and Zhuo Mao of Mi District.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day an edict ordered licentious shrines in commanderies and kingdoms destroyed, keeping only those of King Huan of Luoyang and Zhuo Mao of Mi.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙戌，太尉楊秉薨。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day bingxu, Grand Commandant Yang Bing died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingxu day, Grand Commandant Yang Bing died.

sentences.zh: 秉為人，清白寡慾，嘗稱「我有三不惑：酒、色、財也。

translations.literal: Bing as a man was pure and of few desires; he once said: "I have three things I am not confused by: wine, women, and wealth."
translations.idiomatic: Bing was pure and of few desires; he once said, "I have three things I do not indulge: wine, women, and wealth."

sentences.zh: 秉既沒，所舉賢良廣陵劉瑜乃至京師上書言：「中官不當比肩裂土，競立胤嗣，繼體傳爵。

translations.literal: After Bing's death, the worthy man he had recommended, Liu Yu of Guangling, reached the capital and submitted a memorial: "Palace officials should not stand shoulder to shoulder with princes who divide the land, competing to establish heirs and succeeding generations in transmission of nobility."
translations.idiomatic: After Bing's death, Liu Yu of Guangling, whom he had recommended, reached the capital and memorialized: "Palace officials should not stand beside princes who hold fiefs, competing to set up heirs and pass down noble titles."

sentences.zh: 又，嬖女充積，冗食空宮，傷生費國。

translations.literal: Again, favored women fill the palace; redundant eaters empty the palaces—injuring life and wasting the state."
translations.idiomatic: Again, favored women crowd the palace; idle mouths empty the halls—wasting life and draining the state.

sentences.zh: 又，第捨增多，窮極奇巧，掘山攻石，促以嚴刑。

translations.literal: Again, mansions and lodges multiply; exhausted at reaching bizarre ingenuity, they dig mountains and attack stone, driven by harsh punishments."
translations.idiomatic: Again, mansions multiply, pushed to bizarre artifice, digging mountains and quarrying stone under harsh punishment.

sentences.zh: 州郡官府，各自考事，姦情賕賂，皆為吏餌。

translations.literal: Commanderies, districts, and government offices each conduct their own investigations; crafty dealings and bribes all become bait for officials."
translations.idiomatic: Provinces and districts each conduct their own trials; bribery and craft all become bait for officials.

sentences.zh: 民愁鬱結，起入賊黨，官輒興兵誅討其罪。

translations.literal: The people, worried and knotted in grief, rise and enter bandit gangs; officials then raise troops to execute and punish their crimes."
translations.idiomatic: The people, knotted in grief, rise into bandit gangs; officials then raise troops to execute them.

sentences.zh: 貧困之民，或有賣其首級以要酬賞，父兄相代殘身，妻孥相視分裂。

translations.literal: Among the poor there are some who sell their heads for reward; fathers and elder brothers take turns mutilating themselves, wives and children gaze upon one another in dismemberment."
translations.idiomatic: Among the poor some sell heads for bounty; fathers and brothers take turns mutilating themselves, wives and children watch one another torn apart.

sentences.zh: 又，陛下好微行近習之家，私幸宦者之捨，賓客市買，熏灼道路，因此暴縱，無所不容。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty delights in secret outings to the homes of close attendants, in private visits to eunuchs' quarters, where guests buy and sell in the markets—their smoke and heat scorching the roads; through this, violent indulgence is allowed, and nothing is forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty delights in secret outings to the homes of close attendants and in private visits to eunuchs' quarters, where guests trade in the markets until smoke and clamor scorch the roads; through this, violent indulgence goes unchecked and nothing is forbidden.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下開廣諫道，博觀前古，遠佞邪之人，放鄭、衛之聲，則政致和平，德感祥風矣。

translations.literal: Only if Your Majesty opens wide the path of remonstrance, broadly observes the former ancients, keeps far from flatterers and the wicked, and dismisses the music of Zheng and Wei will government reach peace and virtue move auspicious winds.
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty opens wide the path of remonstrance, broadly surveys the former ancients, keeps far from flatterers and the wicked, and dismisses the licentious music of Zheng and Wei will government reach peace and virtue summon auspicious winds.

sentences.zh: 」詔特召瑜問災咎之征。

translations.literal: " An edict specially summoned Yu to inquire into the signs of disaster and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict specially summoned Yu to inquire into the signs of disaster and calamity.

sentences.zh: 執政者欲令瑜依違其辭，乃更策以它事，瑜復悉心對八千餘言，有切於前，拜為議郎。

translations.literal: Those in power wished to make Yu equivocate in his words; they therefore changed the topic and questioned him on other matters. Yu again answered with full care in more than eight thousand words, sharper than before, and was appointed Gentleman Consultant.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power wished to make Yu equivocate; they therefore changed the topic and questioned him on other matters. Yu again answered with full care in more than eight thousand words, sharper than before, and was appointed Gentleman Consultant.

sentences.zh: 荊州兵朱蓋等叛，與桂陽賊胡蘭等復攻桂陽，太守任胤棄城走，賊眾遂至數萬。

translations.literal: The Jing Province soldiers Zhu Gai and others rebelled; joining with the Guiyang bandits Hu Lan and others, they again attacked Guiyang. The Administrator Ren Yin abandoned the city and fled, and the bandit force soon reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Province soldiers under Zhu Gai rebelled; joining the Guiyang bandits Hu Lan and others, they again attacked Guiyang. Administrator Ren Yin abandoned the city and fled, and the rebel force soon numbered tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 轉攻零陵，太守下邳陳球固守拒之。

translations.literal: They then turned to attack Lingling; the Administrator Chen Qiu of Xiapi held firm and resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: They then turned to attack Lingling; Administrator Chen Qiu of Xiapi held firm and resisted them.

sentences.zh: 零陵下濕，編木為城，郡中惶恐。

translations.literal: Lingling lay low and damp; they wove wood into walls, and throughout the commandery there was fear and alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Lingling lay low and damp; they wove wood into walls, and fear spread through the commandery.

sentences.zh: 掾史白球遣家避難，球怒曰：「太守分國虎符，受任一邦，豈顧妻孥而沮國威乎！

translations.literal: A clerk told Qiu to send his family away to safety. Qiu angrily said, "The Administrator shares the state's tiger tally and receives charge of a whole province—how could he look to wife and children and thus dampen the state's authority!
translations.idiomatic: A clerk urged Qiu to send his family away to safety. Qiu angrily said, "The Administrator shares the state's tiger tally and holds charge of a whole province—how could he think of wife and children and thus weaken the state's authority!

sentences.zh: 復言者斬！

translations.literal: Whoever speaks of this again shall be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: Whoever speaks of this again shall be beheaded!

sentences.zh: 」乃弦大木為方，羽矛為矢，引機發之，多所殺傷。

translations.literal: " He then strung great logs into frames, used feathered spears as bolts, drew the mechanisms and released them, and killed and wounded many.
translations.idiomatic: " He then strung great logs into frames, used feathered spears as projectiles, drew the mechanisms and released them, and killed and wounded many.

sentences.zh: 賊激流灌城，球輒於內因地勢，反決水淹賊，相拒十餘日不能下。

translations.literal: The bandits diverted rushing water to flood the city; Qiu, within the walls, used the terrain to turn the water back and drown the bandits. They resisted each other for more than ten days without the city being taken.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits diverted rushing water to flood the city; Qiu, within the walls, used the terrain to turn the water back and drown the bandits. They held each other off for more than ten days without the city falling.

sentences.zh: 時度尚征還京師，詔以尚為中郎將，率步騎二萬餘人救球，發諸郡兵並勢討擊，大破之，斬蘭等首三千餘級，復以尚為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: At this time Du Shang returned from campaign to the capital. An edict appointed Shang General of the Gentlemen of the Household and ordered him to lead more than twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to rescue Qiu, mobilizing troops from the various commanderies to join forces in attack. He inflicted a great defeat, beheaded more than three thousand of Hu Lan and the others, and Shang was again made Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Du Shang returned from campaign to the capital. An edict appointed him General of the Gentlemen of the Household and ordered him to lead more than twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to rescue Qiu, mobilizing troops from the commanderies for a combined attack. He inflicted a great defeat, beheading more than three thousand of Hu Lan and the others, and Shang was again made Inspector of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧太守張敘為賊所執，及任胤皆征棄市。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Cangwu Zhang Xu was seized by the bandits; he and Ren Yin were both summoned and executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Cangwu Administrator Zhang Xu was seized by the bandits; he and Ren Yin were both summoned and executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 胡蘭餘黨南走蒼梧，交趾刺史張磐擊破之，賊復還入荊州界。

translations.literal: The remnant followers of Hu Lan fled south to Cangwu; the Inspector of Jiaozhi Zhang Pan defeated them, but the bandits again re-entered the borders of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Lan's remnant followers fled south to Cangwu; Jiaozhi Inspector Zhang Pan defeated them, but the bandits again crossed back into Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 度尚懼為己負，乃偽上言蒼梧賊入荊州界，於是征磐下廷尉。

translations.literal: Du Shang, fearing that he would be held responsible, falsely submitted a memorial saying that the Cangwu bandits had entered Jing Province; Zhang Pan was therefore summoned and sent down to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shang, fearing he would be held responsible, falsely memorialized that the Cangwu bandits had entered Jing Province; Zhang Pan was therefore summoned and sent to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 辭狀未正，會赦見原，磐不肯出獄，方更牢持械節。

translations.literal: The case had not yet been decided when an amnesty arrived and he was pardoned, but Pan refused to leave prison and only tightened his grip on his fetters and staff.
translations.idiomatic: The case had not yet been decided when an amnesty arrived and he was pardoned, but Pan refused to leave prison and only tightened his grip on his fetters and staff of office.

sentences.zh: 獄吏謂磐曰：「天恩曠然，而君不出，何乎？

translations.literal: The prison officer said to Pan, "Heaven's grace is broad and clear—yet you do not leave. Why?
translations.idiomatic: The prison officer said to Pan, "Heaven's grace is broad and clear—yet you do not leave. Why?

sentences.zh: 」磐曰：「磐備位方伯，為尚所枉，受罪牢獄。

translations.literal: " Pan said, "Pan holds the post of a regional lord, was wronged by Shang, and suffers punishment in prison.
translations.idiomatic: " Pan said, "Pan holds the post of a regional lord, was wronged by Shang, and suffers punishment in prison.

sentences.zh: 夫事有虛實，法有是非，磐實不辜，赦無所除；

translations.literal: Affairs have truth and falsehood, and law has right and wrong; Pan is in truth innocent, and the amnesty removes nothing;
translations.idiomatic: Affairs have truth and falsehood, and law has right and wrong; Pan is in truth innocent, and the amnesty removes nothing;

sentences.zh: 如忍以苟免，永受侵辱之恥，生為惡吏，死為敝鬼。

translations.literal: if I endure this to gain release, I shall forever bear the shame of insult; alive I would be a wicked official, dead a broken ghost.
translations.idiomatic: if I endure this to gain release, I shall forever bear the shame of insult; alive I would be a wicked official, dead a broken ghost.

sentences.zh: 乞傳尚詣廷尉，面對曲直，足明真偽。

translations.literal: I beg that Shang be summoned to the Minister of Justice so that right and wrong may be faced directly and truth and falsehood fully made clear.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Shang be summoned to the Minister of Justice so that right and wrong may be faced directly and truth and falsehood fully made clear.

sentences.zh: 尚不征者，磐埋骨牢檻，終不虛出，望塵受枉！

translations.literal: If Shang is not summoned, Pan will bury his bones in prison bars and never leave on false grounds, looking to the dust while suffering injustice!
translations.idiomatic: If Shang is not summoned, Pan will bury his bones behind prison bars and never leave on false grounds, looking to the dust while suffering injustice!

sentences.zh: 」廷尉以其狀上，詔書征尚，到廷尉，辭窮，受罪，以先有功得原。

translations.literal: " The Minister of Justice submitted his statement upward; an edict summoned Shang. When he reached the Minister of Justice his words were exhausted, he received punishment, and because of earlier merit was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: " The Minister of Justice submitted his statement upward; an edict summoned Shang. When he reached the Minister of Justice his case collapsed, he received punishment, and because of earlier merit was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 閏月，甲午，南宮朔平署火。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the day jiawu, the Shuo-ping Office of the Southern Palace caught fire.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on jiawu day, the Shuo-ping Office of the Southern Palace caught fire.

sentences.zh: 段熲擊破西羌，進兵窮追，展轉山谷間，自春及秋，無日不戰，虜遂敗散，凡斬首二萬三千級，獲生口數萬人，降者萬餘落。

translations.literal: Duan Jiong defeated the Western Qiang, advanced his army in relentless pursuit, and turned back and forth among the mountain valleys. From spring through autumn there was not a day without battle; the barbarians were defeated and scattered. In all, heads cut numbered twenty-three thousand; captives taken numbered tens of thousands, and those who surrendered numbered more than ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jiong defeated the Western Qiang and pursued them relentlessly through the mountain valleys. From spring through autumn there was not a day without battle; the enemy was defeated and scattered. In all, twenty-three thousand heads were taken; tens of thousands were captured alive, and more than ten thousand households surrendered.

sentences.zh: 封熲都鄉侯。

translations.literal: Jiong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Duxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was enfeoffed as Marquis of Duxiang.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，以太史大夫陳蕃為太尉。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the Grand Master of Writing Chen Fan was made Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Grand Master of Writing Chen Fan was made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 蕃讓於太常胡廣、議郎王暢、弛刑徒李膺，帝不許。

translations.literal: Fan yielded the post to Minister of Ceremonies Hu Guang, Gentleman Consultant Wang Chang, and remitted convict Li Ying; the Emperor did not consent.
